messages:
alex_k: FYI I'm seeing a big provisioner failure window in us-west2 starting ~02:12 UTC — GPU node boots fail because apiserver connections are being dropped.
maria_s: Same. apiserver 5xx spike and controller-manager leader flips. Provisioner can't talk to apiserver to update Node status.
sam_t: Error from provisioner logs: `dial tcp x.x.x.x:6443: i/o timeout` repeated. Traced to NAT node SNAT port exhaustion on our private clusters in the region.
lee_ops: Confirmed on VPC NAT metrics — SNAT port utilization hit 65534 on several NAT instances around 02:10. Connections started failing.
alex_k: Quick repro: curl to apiserver from a worker hits ephemeral port exhaustion on the NAT -> client connections drop, kubelet -> apiserver keep failing and controller-manager goes into leader election.
priya_r: Oof. That explains the controller-manager restarts -- it can't renew leases because of failed calls. Rolling back some recent kube-proxy changes doesn't help.
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT logged INC-2026-031 by @alex_k — apiserver connection failures in us-west2 affecting GPU provisioning :rotating_light:
maria_s: Short-term mitigation options: 1) increase NAT instance count / use larger NAT (costy), 2) per-node hairpin / egress SNAT on nodes (complex), 3) throttle provisioner concurrency to reduce connections.
lee_ops: We can also enable connection reuse on the provisioner (keepalive) — that'll reduce ephemeral ports used per pod creation. But that requires a quick patch and rollout.
sam_t: I'm in favor of throttling provisioner concurrently while we push fixes. Set concurrency to 4 for GPU pools? Current is 20.
alex_k: Agree. Throttling buys time. I'm going to set provisioner max parallel to 4 and reduce burst until midnight UTC. Oncall will monitor.
priya_r: For medium term we should add NAT gateway autoscaling (or switch to managed NAT) — estimate ~+$2.3k/month for us-west2 peak to avoid this class of failure.
maria_s: Also add a fallback route: in the short-term we can route outbound control-plane traffic through dedicated NATs for control-plane endpoints only, isolate provisioning traffic.
lee_ops: Patch plan: 1) throttle provisioner -> live at 02:35 (alex) 2) deploy keepalive patch branch to provisioner-canary -> 02:50 (sam) 3) scale up NAT instances by 2 -> 03:05 (lee). I'll run the NAT scale now.
sam_t: Keepalive patch ready in a small container image; will push to canary namespace in ~10m and watch for SNAT port drop.
alex_k: Doing the throttle now: `kubectl -n infra patch cm provisioner-config --patch '{"data":{"parallelProvisioners":"4"}}'`
lee_ops: NAT scaled +2, seeing SNAT port util drop to ~40% on the scaled instances — connections returning. apiserver 5xxs are decreasing.
oncall-bot: Monitor alert: apiserver 5xx rate falls below threshold — auto-update in 2m.
priya_r: Cost note: switching to managed NAT permanently adds cost but will save incidents and operational toil. I'll open a PR with a 3-month cost comparison and ROI.
maria_s: After we stabilize let's add a circuit-breaker on provisioner side: if apiserver error rate > X, backoff and requeue. Avoid thundering herd.
sam_t: Agreed. Also adding connection pooling for client-go should be high priority — it's cheap and reduces ephemeral ports per worker.
alex_k: Action items
- alex_k: throttle provisioner -> done
- lee_ops: NAT scale -> done
- sam_t: deploy keepalive canary -> in progress
- priya_r: PR for managed NAT cost analysis -> assigned
- maria_s: add circuit-breaker + rollback plan -> assigned
Please ack if you're on it. :thumbsup:
maria_s: ack
sam_t: ack
lee_ops: ack
priya_r: ack
alex_k: I'll keep this thread updated; will push follow-up incident postmortem once we have timeline + root cause confirmed.
